authors.name: Cesar Adib Majul
authors.bio: Cesar Adib Majul was a Philippine historian best known for his work on the history of Islam in the Philippines, and on the life of Apolinario Mabini.

authors.name: Najeeb M. Saleeby
authors.bio: Lebanese-born American physician who served the Moro Province as superintendent of schools and agent for Moro affairs, and read the sultanates’ own tarsilas to write the first histories of them in English.

authors.name: Peter G. Gowing
authors.bio: American church historian who founded the Dansalan Research Center in Marawi City in 1971 and wrote the standard account of American rule over the Moros.

authors.name: James Francis Warren
authors.bio: Australian historian of Southeast Asia at Murdoch University, whose studies of the Sulu Zone made the sultanate’s trading and raiding world a field of its own.

authors.name: Samuel K. Tan
authors.bio: Samuel Kong Tan was a Filipino historian, academic and author. He has headed various cultural institutions including the National Historical Institute and the National Commission for Culture and the Arts.

authors.name: Ruurdje Laarhoven
authors.bio: Dutch historian who worked the Dutch East India Company’s archives for the seventeenth-century Maguindanao sultanate.

authors.name: Reynaldo C. Ileto
authors.bio: Reynaldo "Rey" Clemeña Ileto is a Filipino historian known for his seminal work Pasyon and Revolution: Popular Movements in the Philippines, 1840–1910, first published in 1979. Ileto specializes in Asian history, religion and society, postcolonial studies, and the government and politics of Asia and the Pacific. He is known for his interdisciplinary approach combining history, literature, anthropology, cultural studies, and politics.

authors.name: Patricio N. Abinales
authors.bio: Filipino political scientist at the University of Hawaiʻi at Mānoa, from Ozamiz, who has written on Mindanao’s place in the Philippine state and on the Moro narrative.

authors.name: Shinzo Hayase
authors.bio: Japanese historian of Mindanao and maritime Southeast Asia at Waseda University.

authors.name: Miguel A. Bernad
authors.bio: Miguel Anselmo Azcona Bernad, S.J. was a Filipino Jesuit priest, educator, linguist, critic, academic, historian, author, journalist and editor. Son of Misamis Mayor and Misamis Occidental Governor Don Anselmo Bernad, he entered the Society of Jesus on June 7, 1932 and was ordained March 24, 1946 in the Fordham University Church. He was editor-in-chief of Philippine Studies from 1956 to 1959 and founder of Kinaadman Journal Research Office in 1979.

authors.name: Mamitua Saber
authors.bio: Maranao sociologist who founded Mindanao State University’s University Research Center and the Aga Khan Museum of Islamic Arts in Marawi City, and wrote on Maranao history and art.

authors.name: Ghislaine Loyré
authors.bio: French ethnologist and historian of Maguindanao and of Islam in the Philippines.

authors.name: Nasser A. Marohomsalic
authors.bio: Maranao lawyer and writer, later a commissioner of the Commission on Human Rights, whose self-published history of the Bangsamoro is widely read in the region.

authors.name: B. R. (Rudy) Rodil
authors.bio: Mindanao historian, long of MSU-Iligan Institute of Technology, who sat on the government panels that negotiated with the MNLF and the MILF and has written the region’s history for the general reader.

authors.name: T. J. S. George
authors.bio: Thayil Jacob Sony George was an Indian writer and biographer who received a Padma Bhushan award in 2011 in the field of literature and education.

authors.name: W. K. Che Man
authors.bio: Malaysian political scientist who compared the Moro and Patani Malay movements.

authors.name: Vic Hurley
authors.bio: Gerald Victor Hurley (1898–1978) was a record-breaking athlete, adventurer, expert on the Philippine Islands, military officer, and prolific author. His published books include a non-fiction series relating to the Philippine Islands in the first third of the twentieth century, military histories, screenplays, articles and works of fiction.

authors.name: Sydney A. Cloman
authors.bio: United States Army officer posted to Sulu in the first years of American rule, who wrote a memoir of it two decades later.

authors.name: Robert A. Fulton
authors.bio: American independent historian of the Moro Province, who publishes under his own imprint.

authors.name: James R. Arnold
authors.bio: American military historian and the author of many campaign histories.

authors.name: Michael C. Hawkins

authors.name: Ronald K. Edgerton
authors.bio: Historian, emeritus of the University of Northern Colorado, who has written on central Mindanao and on Pershing’s years among the Moros.

authors.name: Oliver Charbonneau
authors.bio: Historian of American empire at the University of Glasgow.

authors.name: Thomas M. McKenna

authors.name: Asreemoro

authors.name: Ben J. Kadil

authors.name: Clemencio M. Bascar

authors.name: Glenda M. Gloria

authors.name: Salah Jubair (Mohagher Iqbal)

authors.name: Michael O. Mastura

authors.name: Aida Rivera-Ford
authors.bio: Short story writer born in Jolo, Sulu, best known for “The Chieftest Mourner”. She studied at Silliman University, edited its literary magazine Sands and Coral, and made her life in Davao, where she founded the Ford Academy of the Arts, the first fine arts school in Mindanao. She died in January 2026, days before her hundredth birthday.

authors.name: Jaime An Lim
